statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains low because the day's range still contains price after a completed round trip, while stress stays high across the energy, rates and trade channels.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON, with a narrow flagged window from 13:30 to 15:00 UTC covering the post-holiday US cash reopen. Tail sits well below the block threshold; the elevated readings are concentrated in stress rather than in a persistent no-retracement price path.
headline: Nasdaq-100 reopens after Labor Day with NQ mid-range and semis leading, while Brent near $98 and fresh Canadian tariffs keep stress high
body: NQ futures trade near 29,653, up 0.30% on the session, inside a day range of 29,478.00 to 29,764.75. The overnight high was made, retraced and only partly rebuilt, so price sits in the upper half of the range rather than pinned at an extreme. That intact retracement mechanism is the central reason tail risk stays low: mean reversion is visibly still working rather than failing. VIX at 15.40 is below its 15.94 session high, and the 10-year yield at 4.762% is down 0.022 on the day, so the rates channel is not amplifying the equity move. Stress is a separate matter and stays high. WTI trades near $93 and Brent near $98, a six-week high, after Houthi attacks on Saudi energy facilities; elevated energy costs sharpen the significance of this week's PPI and CPI releases. Canada's retaliatory tariffs of 15% to 50% on roughly $20 billion of US goods took effect at 04:01 UTC, reopening the North American trade channel. Index internals are split: semiconductors led the latest session broadly while megacaps were mixed, and Dow futures near -0.6% sit against a positive NQ, which is why the dominant mode is mixed. The narrow flagged window covers the 13:30 UTC post-holiday cash reopen, where two sessions of order flow concentrate into one auction; that reopen has just begun and its structure is not yet observable in the price read above. Beyond it, the 15:00 UTC NY Fed inflation expectations print and the 17:00 UTC 3-year auction are checkpoints rather than observed structure.

lookbackSummary: Across the last 24 hours the assessment stayed in the EA_ON band with tail between 5 and 10 and no reading near the block threshold. Stress climbed from the mid-50s during Monday's Labor Day holiday session to 70 this morning as crude extended on the Saudi facility strikes and the trade channel reopened, while the dominant mode moved from normal to mixed as cross-asset signals kept diverging from Nasdaq price action. The 09:00 UTC slot has no published assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The near-term focus is the 13:30 UTC post-holiday US cash reopen, where two sessions of concentrated order flow lift conditional tail into the low teens for the first two cash hours before easing through the midday lull, the 15:00 UTC NY Fed inflation expectations print and the 17:00 UTC 3-year auction. Conditional tail steps up again into the 20:00 UTC closing auction and then falls to the floor of the horizon overnight. Two channels could produce a step change in either direction: Middle East energy headlines, which carry both a supply-disruption strand and a reported Iran-Oman arrangement on Strait of Hormuz traffic, and yen positioning into the 17-18 September Bank of Japan meeting. The European open at 07:00 UTC on 9 September is the next scheduled flow checkpoint, and PPI on 10 September, CPI on 11 September and the 15-16 September FOMC meeting form the event stack that lifts conditional tail modestly at the end of the horizon.

Price sat mid-to-upper range rather than at an extreme, VIX 15.40 below its 15.94 high, 10-year 4.762% and lower. The 13:30 UTC reopen has just begun; its structure is not yet observable.

forecast.analysis: First full cash hour after the Labor Day break. Conditional tail is a touch higher because post-holiday opening auctions can carry directional flow for longer than usual. It would only become a genuine tail event if pullbacks stayed shallow and the opening range held as support or resistance without a completed retracement.
drivers: First full US cash hour; opening-auction imbalance can extend before it mean-reverts
Invalidation: a completed retracement back through the opening range would cap tail

forecast.analysis: The 15:00 UTC NY Fed Consumer Inflation Expectations release lands in this hour. It is a medium-impact print that mainly informs the rates and inflation narrative; on the evidence available now it is a checkpoint rather than a source of persistent one-way structure.
drivers: 15:00 UTC NY Fed Consumer Inflation Expectations (Aug), medium impact
Oil-driven inflation expectations are the channel most likely to move yields
Tail stays conditional: no observed no-retracement structure is assumed for this hour

forecast.analysis: Midday lull typically follows the opening two hours, with narrowing ranges and better two-way flow. Conditional tail eases accordingly. A rebuild would require the session to leave its midday balance in one direction without retracing.
drivers: Midday balance usually restores two-way flow and supports mean reversion
Conditional easing assumes no fresh Middle East energy headline
Watch whether the day's range holds rather than extends

forecast.analysis: The 17:00 UTC US 3-Year Note Auction sits in this hour. A poor auction transmits through the front end and can pressure duration-sensitive tech, but a single medium-impact auction rarely produces the persistent no-retracement path that defines tail risk.
drivers: 17:00 UTC US 3-Year Note Auction; front-end demand is the transmission channel
Auction tails feed yields first, equities second, usually with retracement
Stress stays high on the unchanged energy and trade backdrop

forecast.analysis: Post-auction afternoon is normally the quietest stretch of the US session. Conditional tail is at the low end of the day, with the assessment framed on the assumption that the auction clears without a disorderly yield move.
drivers: Quiet post-auction window historically supports range behaviour
Assumption: no disorderly front-end repricing after the 3-year auction
Energy remains the dominant stress channel rather than a tail channel

drivers: 19:00 UTC Consumer Credit Change (Jul); low market salience
Late-session positioning begins ahead of the 20:00 UTC cash close
Conditional, not observed: no late-day trend is assumed at this point

forecast.analysis: Final cash hour into the 20:00 UTC close. Index rebalancing and closing imbalances can produce short directional bursts. These are usually resolved rather than persistent, so conditional tail rises modestly and stays well inside the low band.
drivers: 20:00 UTC cash close; closing imbalances can create brief one-way bursts
Closing-auction moves typically resolve rather than extend into the evening
A close near a session extreme would be the signal to reassess, if it occurred

forecast.analysis: After the cash close, futures liquidity thins and the day's range usually stops expanding. Conditional tail falls back as the primary flow driver leaves the market for the evening.
drivers: Post-close futures liquidity thins and range expansion usually stops
Evening session is normally headline-driven rather than flow-driven
Any reassessment would need a fresh energy or geopolitical headline

forecast.analysis: Evening gap between the US close and the Asian open. This is normally the lowest-activity hour of the 24-hour cycle, and conditional tail is set at the floor of the horizon accordingly.
drivers: Lowest-liquidity window between the US close and the Asia open
No scheduled US macro release falls in this hour

forecast.analysis: Tokyo comes online toward the end of this hour. Yen direction into the 17-18 September Bank of Japan meeting is the channel most capable of importing volatility into Nasdaq futures overnight, though it is a stress channel first.
drivers: Tokyo open approaches; yen is the main overnight transmission channel
BoJ meeting on 17-18 September keeps yen positioning a live theme
Yen moves usually raise stress before they raise tail

forecast.analysis: Full Asian session. Regional energy importers are the most exposed to the crude move, so Asian equity tone is one way the oil story can feed back into Nasdaq futures. Any such feedback would be conditional and is not assumed here.
drivers: Asian energy importers are most exposed to the Brent move toward $98
Conditional feedback loop: Asian tone into Nasdaq futures, not yet observed
